name: Lumiere Green
lede: Lumiere Green is a pale yellow-green from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, rare in our painting archive but matched in a Dutch still life painted 270 years before the name existed.

sections.title: A pale yellow-green, with a paler child
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas carries this tone on plate XVII, hue 29′, notated 2.8GY 8.2/5.9 in the Munsell system [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary groups it under block 119, naming it light yellow green, 3.6 units from Ridgway's reading, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists the same swatch on plate 18, I 5 [1].

Its closest neighbors in our library are [[oil-yellow]], about 3.6 units away and more vivid, and [[viridine-green]] and [[pale-lime]], each about 3.9 units off and lighter [2]. Our data also files a paler child variant, [[pale-lumiere-green]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive matches this tone in only 34 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.14 percent, as photographed, rarer than 59 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.5 percent of the 1,674 paintings from that decade, 3.6 times its museums' expected rate [3].

Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 60 percent of its 25 clearly-ranked appearances, a rank computed within each canvas so varnish cannot fake it [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1642 still life by Gerret Willemsz Heda, 270 years before the name itself was recorded in 1912, a reminder that the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of any pigment or dye, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

origin.first_recorded: 1912 (Ridgway); carried into the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary and the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary
origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature; ISCC-NBS, NBS Circular 553; Maerz and Paul, A Dictionary of Color
